item.title: 2027: Defeating Tinubu in 12 states is wishful thinking – Lagos APC tells Makinde
item.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has dismissed the claim by Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s campaign organisation that it will defeat President Bola Tinubu in 12 states in the 2027 presidential election. APC described the declaration as grandiose, wishful thinking and political bravado without electoral evidence. Lagos APC Spokesman, Seye Oladejo, reacting to the claim said participation in an election is not a guarantee of victory. According to him, “Governor Makinde and his campaign team appear to have mistaken the privilege of participating in an election for the guarantee of victory. In the Olympics, participation is celebrated, but no athlete earns a gold medal merely for showing up at the starting line,” the Lagos APC said. The party said the 2027 presidential election is not a theatrical performance rewarded for loudest declarations, noting that it demands national reach, organisational depth, credible structures and capacity to mobilise voters across the federation. “On these fundamental indices, Makinde’s boast raises more questions about the foundations of his confidence than it offers evidence of his electoral strength. Where is the demonstrable national structure? What coalition of enduring value has he assembled?” APC queried. It said Makinde should be more concerned about political crises within his own political family in Oyo State and his unravelling relationships with erstwhile allies, rather than projecting national invincibility. “A politician who has yet to convincingly demonstrate enduring cohesion within his immediate political environment should be cautious about presenting himself as the architect of a nationwide electoral upset,” it said. The party said President Tinubu brings decades of political experience, formidable national network and proven capacity for coalition-building to the 2027 contest, attributes which cannot be wished away by announcing a dozen states. It added that Nigerians will judge platforms on ideas, records and vision, stressing that opposition must do more than announce states it intends to win. “Makinde’s declaration sounds less like a carefully reasoned electoral forecast and more like an attempt to manufacture momentum through headline-grabbing bravado. It is political confidence without sufficiently demonstrated evidence,” the party said. The Lagos APC advised Makinde to spend less time counting imaginary victories and more time examining political turbulence around him, noting that ballot presence does not equal mandate. “After all, in the ultimate reckoning of democracy, the electorate awards the medals, not campaign organisations intoxicated by their own declarations,” Oladejo said. item.title: Edo tanker explosion: NUPENG grieves over loss of lives, calls for sweeping safety reforms
item.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young The Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers, NUPENG, has expressed profound sorrow over the deadly tanker explosion at Oluku, along the Benin-Lagos Highway in Ovia North-East Local Government Area of Edo State, raising fresh concerns over road safety, deteriorating highway conditions and the persistent dangers associated with scooping spilled fuel at accident scenes. The union, in a condolence message to Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, and the people of Oluku community, called for sustained preventive measures to avert similar tragedies, stressing the need for improved road infrastructure, heightened public awareness and stronger collaboration among government agencies and other stakeholders to protect lives and property. In a statement signed by its Acting General Secretary, Comrade Otite Onohwohwo, NUPENG said: “The Nigeria Union of Petroleum and Natural Gas Workers, NUPENG, is profoundly saddened by the tragic tanker explosion that occurred at Oluku along the Benin-Lagos Highway, Ovia North East Local Government Area, Edo State, on Thursday, 15th October 2026. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to His Excellency, Governor Monday Okpebholo, and to the people of Oluku community in Ovia North East Local Government Area, Edo State. “The loss of lives, the injuries sustained, and the destruction of properties in this incident have left our Union’s leadership and membership in a state of collective mourning. We offer our full solidarity to the affected families and communities, and we pray for the repose of the souls of the departed and the swift healing of the injured. “In line with our role as a responsible organization, NUPENG reaffirms its dedication to supporting the Edo State Government and all stakeholders in implementing effective preventive measures. “We emphasize that this disaster underscores the critical necessity for immediate and sustained action to address the deteriorating state of key roadways, especially in Edo State and across the nation as a whole. “It is disheartening that such fatal events continue to occur despite our ongoing collaborative efforts with safety agencies to educate the public on the dangers of interfering with accident scenes through the scooping of spilled fuel and other flammable substances. “NUPENG salutes the efforts of first responders and medical personnel for their prompt intervention. “NUPENG remains steadfast in its pursuit of a safer transportation ecosystem and calls upon all Nigerians to prioritize safety and maintain vigilance. A concerted effort is essential to eradicate these preventable tragedies. “Our solidarity remains constant, for the Union makes us strong!” The post Edo tanker explosion: NUPENG grieves over loss of lives, calls for sweeping safety reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: EU To Offer €20m Defence Support For Nigerian Armed Forces
item.description: The European Union (EU) is planning to provide €20 million in defence assistance to the Armed Forces of Nigeria (AFN) under the European Peace Facility. The proposed support was discussed when the Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. In a statement on Saturday, the minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said an EU technical delegation would visit Abuja in November to agree on the details of the assistance. The meeting also reviewed security cooperation between Nigeria and the EU, with Mignot commending Musa’s efforts to improve the country’s security situation. The ambassador also invited the minister to a meeting of defence ministers in Brussels later this year. The Minister of Defence, Christopher Musa, met with the EU Ambassador to Nigeria and ECOWAS, Gautier Mignot, at Ship House in Abuja. Musa thanked the EU for its continued support and reaffirmed President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to protecting lives and promoting national development. He said relative peace was gradually returning to troubled parts of the country through the efforts of the armed forces and other security agencies, although kidnapping along major highways and attacks on isolated communities remained a challenge. The minister also disclosed that Nigeria was expecting the delivery of 10 attack helicopters, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and other military equipment to strengthen security operations. On regional security, Musa identified the shrinking of the Lake Chad Basin, which supports more than 50 million people, as a potential source of instability. He said denying terrorists access to holding areas on the Lake Chad islands remained a key operational priority for the Multinational Joint Task Force. On the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration (DDR) programme, the minister stressed that the initiative should prioritise victims of the conflict, including affected military personnel. Mignot also commended a recent conference of past and present MNJTF force commanders, attended by representatives of the African Union and the Lake Chad Basin Commission. item.title: SEHRB, Intersociety allege killings, torture in South-East
item.description: By Chinedu Adonu ENUGU — A coalition of human rights organisations has called for an independent investigation into alleged killings, torture, enforced disappearances, secret burials and deaths in custody linked to security operations in South-East Nigeria. The coalition, comprising the South-East Human Rights Bureau (SEHRB), Oganihu Igbo Development Foundation and the International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law (Intersociety), also demanded a probe into reports of unidentified bodies in mortuaries in Imo State. Addressing a joint press conference in Enugu on Saturday, the organisations alleged that some detainees had been subjected to prolonged detention without access to their families and lawyers, as well as torture and other forms of inhuman treatment. They expressed concern that persons reportedly arrested in the South-East had been transferred to detention facilities outside the region, including Wawa Barracks in Niger State and custodial centres in Kuje and Suleja, without their families being adequately informed of their whereabouts. “Our position is clear: the State has a duty to protect citizens from violence, but security operations must themselves comply with the law. The family reportedly had not seen Egbom since the incident. Chiamaka also alleged that her brother was beaten during the operation and subsequently died. The coalition demanded that the DSS account for Egbom’s whereabouts and investigate the circumstances surrounding the alleged death of her son. Other testimonies presented by the organisations included allegations of torture, prolonged detention and denial of family contact involving persons reportedly arrested in Owerri, Orlu and other parts of the South-East. The coalition said the allegations, if substantiated, could amount to serious violations of constitutional rights, the Anti-Torture Act 2017 and Nigeria’s international human rights obligations. Probe of unidentified bodies On reports of unidentified bodies in Imo State, the organisations called for independent forensic investigations to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the circumstances surrounding their deaths. They demanded the preservation of mortuary registers, police records, autopsy reports and other relevant evidence, as well as the use of DNA testing where necessary to identify the remains. The organisations, however, condemned killings, abductions and other atrocities allegedly committed by armed separatist elements, criminal gangs and other non-state actors in the region. “There must be no hierarchy of victims,” they said, adding that civilians killed by armed criminals, persons unlawfully killed by security personnel, detainees who disappear in state custody, torture survivors and unidentified dead all deserved truth, justice and accountability. The coalition urged the National Assembly, the Nigerian Bar Association, civil society groups, religious and traditional leaders, and the media to support credible investigations into the allegations. “The missing must be accounted for. The detained must have access to justice. The dead must be identified and treated with dignity,” the organisations said. item.title: Jigawa Fulani community endorses Tinubu, Namadi, APC candidates
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Fulani community in Jigawa State has endorsed President Bola Tinubu, Governor Umar Namadi and all candidates of the All Progressives Congress (APC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The endorsement was announced at a gathering held at the Manpower Development Institute, Dutse, where community members commended the state government for its efforts to promote peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders. Speaking at the event, the community leader, Alhaji Shehu Hadejia, said the decision to support APC candidates was in recognition of the government’s efforts to address the challenges facing livestock farmers across the state. He particularly commended Namadi for establishing the Ministry of Livestock Development and introducing programmes aimed at improving livestock production and reducing conflicts between farmers and herders. According to him, the gazetting of grazing reserves, regular animal vaccination and other livestock development initiatives have helped improve the welfare of herders in the state. Responding, Namadi described the endorsement as a demonstration of the community’s confidence in his administration and the APC-led government. “Today is also another important day for us. Today, the entire Fulani community in Jigawa State is here,” the governor said. “You can see the number of people who came from all over the state. And they were here to endorse Mr President, the governor, and all the APC candidates in Jigawa State.” Namadi reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to improving livestock production through the provision of grazing reserves, watering stations and animal feed. He said the government was also promoting alfalfa cultivation to ensure adequate feed for livestock. “We are ready to provide feeds. We are ready to provide water, hospitals, schools, and everything else for them,” he said. The governor disclosed that his administration had invested about ₦3.1 billion in artificial insemination programmes over the past two to three years to improve cattle breeds and boost milk production. He added that the government had sustained regular animal vaccination programmes to protect livestock against diseases. Namadi also stressed the need for peaceful coexistence between farmers and herders, urging residents to cooperate with security agencies by providing information on individuals threatening peace in their communities. Earlier, the Commissioner for Livestock Development, Professor Salim Mohammed, said the ministry had recorded significant achievements since its establishment. He listed the demarcation of additional grazing reserves, animal vaccination and public sensitisation on peaceful coexistence among measures introduced to strengthen livestock development in the state. item.title: Borno loses billions in infrastructure to metal scavenging — Zulum
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri Borno State Governor, Babagana Umara Zulum, has said the state has lost infrastructure, electrical materials and metals worth billions of naira to metal scavengers, known in Hausa as Ajakuta. Zulum said the losses, alongside other security concerns, informed the state government’s decision to ban scrap metal trading. The governor spoke at the weekend while addressing scrap metal operators, urging them to submit proposals on how they could continue their businesses without contributing to insecurity or damaging public infrastructure. He explained that the ban was imposed in the overall interest of the state and was not intended to deprive operators of their means of livelihood. Zulum said the government had no personal interest in shutting down their businesses, stressing that the restriction was aimed at protecting public assets and strengthening security. “It is deeply concerning to me if one person loses his livelihood for whatever reason in Borno. Believe me, there is nothing I stand to gain from banning scrap metal trade other than addressing the serious security concerns associated with your activities,” he said. The governor disclosed that the state government spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but the wires were subsequently lost to metal scavenging. “We spent more than ₦3 billion to connect an electricity distribution line from Damaturu to Maiduguri, but unfortunately, we lost all the wires to metal scavenging activities,” he said. Zulum also said hundreds of scavengers had been killed while searching for metals in villages that were not yet safe for civilian activities. He added that security intelligence available to the government indicated that insurgents were using scrap metal trading channels to sell looted metals. “We have security intelligence that even the insurgents use your platforms to sell looted metals. So, no responsible government will ignore such intelligence just to be politically correct,” the governor said. Despite the restriction, Zulum granted operators a waiver to evacuate stocks accumulated before the ban from designated locations. The measure, he said, was intended to ease the impact of the restriction on genuine operators while the government addressed the security and infrastructure concerns associated with the trade. item.title: 2027: HPM targets six million votes for Hashim in North-West
item.description: The Hashim Progressive Movement (HPM) has set a target of at least six million votes for Accord Party presidential candidate, Dr Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, across Nigeria’s North-West region in the 2027 general election. Hon. Aminu Aminu, HPM coordinator and Accord’s senatorial candidate for Jigawa Central, announced the target, saying the movement was mobilising supporters across the seven states of Jigawa, Kano, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Sokoto and Zamfara. “We will prove he is our own in this region and the face of the New North,” Aminu said, describing the campaign as an effort to demonstrate Hashim’s connection with the region and his appeal as a presidential candidate with a national outlook. “This is a homecoming. For decades, the North has searched for a leader who understands its people and their challenges while offering a national vision for all Nigerians. We believe Dr Gbenga Hashim represents that possibility,” he said. Aminu said HPM’s mobilisation strategy would involve ward-to-ward and door-to-door engagement, with youth and women mobilisers working alongside Accord’s legislative candidates to strengthen the party’s presidential campaign. The movement plans to link its presidential mobilisation efforts with Accord’s senatorial and House of Representatives candidates to improve coordination and expand grassroots engagement across the region. “We are connecting presidential hope to grassroots reality,” Aminu said. He added that the movement believed voters were seeking practical solutions to insecurity and economic hardship, issues on which Hashim had continued to outline policy proposals. The six-million-vote figure represents HPM’s stated target for the North-West ahead of the 2027 general election. item.title: Road projects: Uba Sani pays ₦2bn in compensation to 865 property owners
item.description: —Zaria, Sabon Gari, Giwa homeowners benefit -Receives ADC heavyweights into APC in Kaduna By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA –THE Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani has paid ₦2 billion in compensation to 865 property owners affected by township road projects in Zaria, Sabon Gari and Giwa. This makes the total sum the Uba Sani administration has paid so far to over ₦6.85 billion in direct compensation to citizens affected by public works — putting people at the centre of infrastructure. The Governor handed over the cheques at Unguwan Iya, Zaria, in the presence of the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Abbas Tajudeen; Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas; former Governor Ramalan Yero, and other senior officials. The payout reflects the administration’s policy of compensating residents before demolition — a clear break from the past, when infrastructure projects often displaced people without redress. With this arrangement, affected property owners along the township road corridors can be relocated or compensated without loss, allowing construction to proceed without delay. This follows the administration’s earlier compensation exercises, including ₦2.85 billion disbursed in February 2026 for road projects across the state, and ₦2 billion paid in July 2026 to about 1,000 victims of the Rigasa-Tudun Wada flood and erosion control project. Speaking after receiving his cheque, one of the beneficiaries from Zaria, Malam Ibrahim Ahmed, said: “For the first time, government paid us before bringing down our properties. We can now find alternative accommodation without suffering. We thank Governor Uba Sani for remembering the common man.” Another beneficiary from Sabon Gari, Hajiya Fatima Suleiman, said “We were afraid when we heard the road would pass through our houses. But today we have received our compensation in full. This is true leadership — development with human face.” Traditional rulers, community leaders and political party leaders described the event as a validation of the link between leadership and compassion. In what some attendees described as “political tsunami”, the event also witnessed a massive defection as Governor Uba Sani received a wave of heavyweights and their thousands of followers into the All Progressives Congress (APC). Leading the defectors from the African Democratic Congress (ADC) were political bigwigs Bashir Sa’idu, Senator Audu Kwari, Hon. Mohammed Sani Bello Mainan Zazzau, Hon. Jafaru Sani, Hon. Mukhtar Hazo, Hon. Bala Alwa’u, Hon. Nasiru Abdullahi Maikano, Hon. Lawal Buba, Hon. Ephraim Iliyasu and others. The defectors cited the Governor’s inclusive leadership, visible infrastructure delivery and people-centred compensation policy as reasons for abandoning the ADC for the APC. The development, according to observers, further consolidates the APC’s dominance in Kaduna North senatorial zone ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: 2027: Ondo targets one million votes for Tinubu — Oke

item.title: Martinez starts for Man Utd after outburst
item.description: Lisandro Martinez was named in Manchester United’s starting line-up to face Leeds on Sunday despite his controversial remarks about the struggling club’s hierarchy. Argentina defender Martinez took aim at United’s powerbrokers following their 2-0 Champions League loss to Atletico Madrid on Tuesday. Martinez claimed United boss Michael Carrick had been left with an under-strength squad. The centre-back criticised technical director Jason Wilcox, saying he had “100 percent” expected more investment during the summer transfer window after United finished third in the Premier League last season. It is understood Martinez, who issued an apology on Thursday, has been fined for his outburst. Carrick confirmed during a pre-match press conference on Friday that Martinez would be in his squad for their Premier League match at bitter rivals Leeds. And he was true to his word as Martinez was selected in a United team looking to win for just the third time in 10 games this term. United have gone five matches without a victory in all competitions and are languishing in 14th place in the Premier League. item.title: I don’t want my son to lose Medicine and Surgery admission — Abia pastor cries out
item.description: …330 UTME score, no N500,000 to secure admission By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — For Rev. Enyinnaya Nwabuko, a rural pastor in one of the foremost Pentecostal churches who has spent nearly two decades preaching the gospel, one prayer now weighs heavily on his heart: that poverty will not destroy his son’s dream of becoming a medical doctor. His son, Marvelous Nwabuko, has secured provisional admission to study Medicine and Surgery at Abia State University (ABSU), Uturu, after scoring an impressive 330 in the 2026 Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination (UTME). But the family’s joy is threatened by a financial hurdle. With nearly ₦500,000 needed to pay the acceptance fee and other initial charges within two weeks, the indigent cleric is appealing to the Abia State Government, philanthropists, corporate organisations and other well-meaning Nigerians to help save his son’s admission. “I don’t want my son to lose his admission because of poverty. That is why I am crying out for help,” the distressed father told Vanguard. A father of three, Nwabuko hails from Umuelem Amakanma in Umuahia South Local Government Area but ministers at a local church, whose name is withheld, in Etorue Oloko, a rural community in Ikwuano LGA. For years, he and his wife have laboured in God’s vineyard, feeding the flock and serving their community despite their modest means. Now, the family faces a test of their faith and needs urgent intervention to avert a looming disappointment. Marvelous’s academic journey makes the prospect of losing the admission particularly painful. Last year, he sat for the UTME for the first time and scored an outstanding 340. However, he was denied admission because he was underage. Undeterred, Marvelous, who will turn 17 on November 10, returned to the JAMB examination hall in 2026, scored 330 and earned another opportunity to pursue his medical ambition. His Senior School Certificate Examination (SSCE) results were equally impressive, with three A1s and six B3s, giving him nine credits in one sitting. Yet, despite his academic brilliance, the young scholar may be unable to cross the threshold of university education simply because his parents cannot raise the required fees on time. “Since he got the admission letter last Friday, the two weeks allowed for payment have started counting. I have approached some people for assistance, but so far, it has been promises,” the father lamented. “I am afraid that if help does not come quickly, he may lose this opportunity. My desire is to give my son the best as a father, but my present financial situation is a challenge.” For Rev. Nwabuko, the appeal goes beyond securing admission. It is a plea to protect the future of a child whose hard work has earned him a place in medical school. He acknowledged that the financial demands of studying Medicine and Surgery extend far beyond acceptance fees and initial charges but said he was determined not to allow his economic circumstances to extinguish his son’s ambition.

item.title: Flamingos lose 2-1 to Poland in U-17 Women’s World Cup opener
item.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos began their campaign at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco with a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening Group B match on Saturday. The match, played at the Mohammed VI Football Complex in Rabat, saw Poland score twice before Nigeria pulled one back late in the second half. Poland took the lead from the spot in the 33rd minute through Wiktoria Skrzypczak before Natalia Skrok doubled the advantage in the 65th minute, finishing a move assisted by Blanka Zajac. The Flamingos responded in the 79th minute when Oluebube Umejiaku converted a pass from Kanyisola Yusuf to reduce the deficit and raise hopes of a comeback. However, Poland held on to secure all three points, leaving Nigeria with a disappointing start to their campaign. Saturday’s encounter was the first meeting between both countries at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Poland have featured at the tournament once before, reaching the quarter-finals in 2024, while Nigeria have established themselves as regular participants. The Flamingos have made eight appearances at the competition, reaching the quarter-finals in 2010, 2012, 2014 and 2024. Nigeria’s best performance came in 2022, when they won the bronze medal. The team lost their semi-final against Colombia on penalties before defeating Germany in the third-place match, also via a shootout. The Nigerian side will now turn their attention to Tuesday’s Group B fixture against Puerto Rico as they seek to recover from the opening defeat and strengthen their chances of reaching the knockout stage. At the Mfum–Ekok corridor, the assessment identified gaps in reliable electricity supply, connectivity, information technology equipment, cybersecurity, technical support, scanner commissioning and coordinated single-stop processing. At Sèmè–Kraké, the challenges included incomplete joint procedures and live data exchange, non-functional cargo-scanning and weighing facilities, unreliable electricity, traffic congestion, inconsistent operating hours and unresolved responsibilities for maintaining shared infrastructure. The NCS said the findings highlighted the need to address immediate operational deficiencies while developing a properly assessed and costed long-term modernisation programme. To advance the initiative, Afreximbank proposed a two-stage approach, beginning with independent engineering assessments and investment-cost studies at the two border posts, followed by the development of separate bankable project packages for the Nigeria–Benin and Nigeria–Cameroon corridors. The proposed project-preparation process would include transaction advisory services, legal due diligence, financial modelling and the identification of appropriate implementation and financing arrangements. The bank also outlined the potential use of its Project Preparation Facility, while technical partners, TMP and Bergmans Security Consultants and Supplies Limited, expressed willingness in principle to consider self-financing the preparatory work. However, the NCS clarified that no final project cost, lending commitment, borrower designation, financing arrangement or implementation contract had been established. Participants agreed on the need for direct site inspections, designated technical focal points, a clear one-, three- and six-month implementation roadmap and a dated action matrix to guide further engagement. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to regional cooperation, border modernisation and the facilitation of legitimate trade in line with AfCFTA objectives. It said it would continue engaging with Customs authorities in Benin and Cameroon, Afreximbank and relevant technical partners to advance the assessments, clarify project-preparation arrangements and develop sustainable solutions for the two border corridors. The initiative is expected to support more efficient cross-border procedures, improve cargo visibility, strengthen coordinated border management and contribute to the development of an integrated African trading environment. item.title: Ukraine Drone Attack Kills One, Sets Two Russian Oil Refineries Ablaze
item.description: A “massive” Ukrainian drone attack overnight killed one person, wounded five others and set two oil refineries ablaze in the Russian city of Saint Petersburg, its governor said Sunday. “One person was killed and five others hurt and hospitalised following a massive attack carried out by Ukrainian Nazi military drones,” governor Alexandre Beglov said. He added firefighters were battling blazes at the Saint Petersburg oil terminal site, also hit in June, the Ruchi oil depot and industrial warehouses in the Kolpino district south of the city. Beglov added several residential buildings had been hit, as well as two houses. “Air defence systems are in operation,” he wrote on Telegram. Smoke rises above the city following an air attack on the oil terminal in Saint Petersburg on October 18, 2026, amid the ongoing Russian-Ukrainian conflict. (Photo by AFP) City authorities said the attack also disrupted flights at Saint Petersburg’s main airport, one of the country’s busiest, which was restricting operations “for safety reasons”, Beglov said. The strikes came after Ukraine’s leader Volodymyr Zelensky said this week Kyiv would resume hitting Russian refineries, after an “energy ceasefire” announced by US President Donald Trump failed to materialise. Zelensky insisted he was standing up for his war-torn country in the face of unrelenting Russian attacks, including on energy infrastructure, as support from the United States slumped. The governor of the Leningrad region surrounding Saint Petersburg, Alexander Drozdenko, said 145 drones had been shot down and said around 20,000 people were without electricity following the drone raid. “A large-scale UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle) attack continues to be repelled,” Drozdenko wrote on Telegram. A police car is parked in front of a burning oil terminal following an air attack in Saint Petersburg on October 18, 2026, amid the ongoing Russian-Ukrainian conflict. (Photo by AFP) Saint Petersburg and the surrounding region are home to major oil infrastructure. Ukraine has specifically targeted the sector over recent months in retaliation for Russian bombings. TASS news agency said the attack was the largest on the region since the start of the war in February 2022. A June 6 attack saw 144 drones shot down, according to officials. Russia’s defence ministry said overall 1,015 Ukrainian drones were neutralised Saturday night in around 15 regions in Russia’s south and west, including the capital, Moscow. The Russian VK social network said the attack targeted one of its data centres in the region but that the site was working as normal. Trump, who has repeatedly criticised Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries and oil depots, signed an executive order on Friday to waive sanctions and tariffs targeting Moscow’s energy revenues. item.title: ‘Record’ 855 People Arrested Over Paris Protest Violence – Police
item.description: Police in Paris said Sunday they had arrested a “record” 855 people over protest violence in the capital the day before, with the prosecutor’s office saying more than 500 were being held in custody. The capital, and many other French cities, on Saturday experienced clashes between police and protesters, multiple street blazes and widespread looting. Paris’s deputy mayor Lamia El Aaraje said the capital had been hit by “a level of violence that I believe we had never seen before”. French gendarmes patrol by a broken frontage windows of a shop a day after riot and looting following a nationwide protest against the “high cost of living”, in Lyon central-eastern France on October 18, 2026. (Photo by JEFF PACHOUD / AFP) The Paris prosecutor’s office said that, of those in custody, 346 were adults and 171 were minors, for a total of 517. It added that the numbers were provisional and could change. “Arrests took place throughout the night and up to 6:00 am (0400 GMT) this morning,” the office said. Most of the arrests were for receiving stolen goods, association with intent to commit violence, and vandalism, it said.
